### Rethinking Local News: How Sarah Alvarez Is Building Journalism in Support of Community Needs
Source: Nieman Reports

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Nieman Reports [media_lens] https://niemanreports.org/local-news-detroit-michigan-public-media-sarah-alvarez-founder-ceo-community-needs-foreclosures-outlier-media-documenters-city-bureau-chicago/

Sarah Alvarez has spent much of her career rethinking how local journalism can serve the public. After working as a civil rights attorney, then as a reporter and producer at the NPR station Michigan Public, she founded Outlier Media in 2016. Alvarez said the Detroit-based nonprofit newsroom was designed to fill information and accountability gaps in communities that were often overlooked by traditional news organizations.. One of its signature innovations, TXT OUTLIER, is a text message service Alvarez created to connect Detroiters directly with journalists and provide practical information on issues affecting their lives, from utility bills to housing and foreclosures. Under Alvarez’s leadership, Outlier also expanded its Documenters program, an initiative that trains and pays residents to attend and report on public meetings to create a public record of local government decisions in places that don’t have press coverage. The initiative has engaged more than 700 Detroiters and since spread nationwide, creating new opportunities for civic participation and public accountability.

With the first U.S. midterm elections since President Donald Trump’s return to the White House approaching, voters will be weighing in on a range of issues, from the economy and rising cost of living, to the administration’s foreign policy and the future direction of both major parties. At a recent virtual Nieman-to-Nieman seminar, a group of Nieman alums who cover politics discussed what they’re hearing from voters with regards to key Senate races, the growing influence of younger voters drawn to progressive candidates, and the political implications of conflicts involving Iran, Ukraine, and Russia. Moderated by Austin Bogues (NF ’21), news desk editor at USA Today, the discussion brought together James Barragán (NF ’24), political anchor for Spectrum News in Austin, Texas; Bill Barrow (NF ’22), national politics reporter for The Associated Press in Atlanta; and Ines Pohl (NF ’05), Washington bureau chief and White House correspondent for Deutsche Welle, Germany’s international public broadcaster.

As protests continue across India over allegations of government corruption, dozens of members of the media have been subjected to arrest, detainment and assault, according to witnesses, press rights organizations, and the journalists themselves. Thousands of protesters have taken to the streets of New Delhi in recent weeks, demanding the resignation of election officials allegedly tied to the deletion of nearly 130 million names from voter registration rolls. The protests — which have largely been organized by the Cockroach Janata Party, so named after India's chief justice called the nation’s unemployed youth and activists "cockroaches" — are part of a wider wave of youth discontent aimed at Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his administration. Organizers have mobilized young people via social media, tapping into frustrations with government corruption, eroding trust in democratic institutions, and a lack of access to jobs and educational opportunities.

The Trump administration’s latest attacks on the news media have followed a familiar pattern: President Donald Trump lashes out at news outlets for perceived bias and follows up with restrictive actions that appear blatantly unconstitutional; a judge’s ruling follows, temporarily halting the actions; and the administration pivots and pushes ahead with other restrictions. This time it was the removal of three outlets — CNN, MS NOW, and Politico — from White House press access in September. After the groups sued, and U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly issued a temporary restraining order restoring their access on Sept. 24, the administration barred CNN and Politico from providing pool coverage on trips outside Washington. Kelly issued a longer, preliminary injunction on Oct. 14, halting the administration from blocking the news organizations’ access to the White House while the case proceeds. Source: Nieman Reports

My happiest times in journalism have been when I have built something new. For my latest venture, I want to help bring investigative journalism on climate and environmental issues to a much larger audience than it has reached in the past. To do so, I’m starting a brand-new newsroom focused on the environmental and climate crisis, and I’m taking my audience along for the ride. I’ll be documenting every facet of the process with an “open kitchen” approach of radical transparency, starting with a 100-day video countdown chronicling all the steps involved with starting a news organization from the ground up. This effort combines two of the things I’m most passionate about: I love digging up stories that other people don’t want to see published, and I love creating opportunities for other journalists. I’ve been a journalist for most of my life. I started working at age 14 for the local paper in my rural German town, turned to doing investigative stories in my early 20s, and later studied investigative journalism at the Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism in New York.

### America’s Shrinking Local Newsrooms, Through a Photographer’s Lens
Source: Nieman Reports
Published: 2026-10-02 12:30 UTC
URL: https://niemanreports.org/americas-shrinking-local-newsrooms-photographer-ann-hermes-local-news-news-deserts-rural-america/
Source meta: reference_tool · aggregator · R3 · P4 · reference
Fetched: 2026-11-18 01:58 UTC

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Nieman Reports [media_lens] https://niemanreports.org/americas-shrinking-local-newsrooms-photographer-ann-hermes-local-news-news-deserts-rural-america/

For many journalists, the sight of empty desks is a sadly familiar one. My first glimpse of a gutted newsroom facing further cutbacks sparked a documentary photography project that has so far taken me to more than 50 newsrooms across the United States over the past eight years. It began when my mother, a loyal subscriber to our local metro in southern Illinois, told me a decade ago how disappointed she was in the newspaper. She complained that the local coverage was lacking, and the paper seemed to be thinner. Already several years into my photojournalism career, I was unsurprised by her remarks — I had been witnessing the decline of print media since graduation from journalism school. Still, my curiosity was piqued, and I arranged a visit to the paper to see for myself. Cue the scene of a barren newsroom. Not only were there empty desks, but also an expanse of exposed carpet with indentations showing where desks had once long stood. While there has been a great deal of reporting on the issues plaguing local journalism, I hadn’t seen the story told visually.

### 澳枪击事件嫌疑人为父子：曾宣誓效忠“伊斯兰国”，行凶枪支为合法持有
Source: The Paper 澎湃新闻
Published: 2025-12-16 02:23 UTC
URL: https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178049
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-18 01:59 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Paper 澎湃新闻 [global_news] https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178049

据新华社12月15日援引澳大利亚广播公司报道，澳大利亚联合反恐小组调查人员表示，悉尼邦迪滩枪击事件两名嫌疑人曾宣誓效忠“伊斯兰国”恐怖组织。 报道援引联合反恐小组一名不愿透露姓名的高级官员的话说，警方在邦迪滩两名枪手车内发现一面“伊斯兰国”旗帜。澳大利亚安全情报组织6年前就已在调查邦迪滩枪击案两名枪手之一的纳维德·阿克拉姆，他与“伊斯兰国”在悉尼的恐怖分子有密切联系。 澳大利亚警方表示，枪击事件的两名嫌疑人是父子关系，使用合法获得的枪支发动了此次袭击事件。 澳大利亚总理阿尔巴尼斯15日表示：“今天下午4点， 我将把更严格的枪支法律列入国家内阁的议程，包括限制个人可持有或许可的枪支数量 。此外，还需对许可证进行定期审查。人们的情况会发生变化，人们的思想也会随着时间的推移而变得激进。许可证不应永久有效。” 此次枪击事件已造成包括1名作案嫌疑人在内的16人死亡、40人受伤。这是自1996年塔斯马尼亚州亚瑟港枪击事件造成35人死亡以来，澳大利亚发生的最严重的大规模枪击事件。 持有枪支许可证长达十年 据多家外媒报道，其中一名袭击者为24岁的澳大利亚公民纳维德·阿克拉姆，他在现场被捕，随后被送往悉尼的一家医院。另一名袭击者是他的父亲萨吉德·阿克拉姆，他于1998年来到澳大利亚，被警方当场击毙。 澳大利亚警方随后证实，纳维德·阿克拉姆此前已被新南威尔士州警方和其他机构记录在案。其父亲萨吉德·阿克拉姆持有枪支许可证，名下登记有6支枪，目前均已被追回。新南威尔士州警察局长马尔·兰永透露，萨吉德·阿克拉姆已持有枪支许可证长达十年。 阿尔巴尼斯在新闻发布会上透露，纳维德·阿克拉姆曾于2019年10月首次引起当局的注意。他补充说，对该男子进行检查是基于他与其他人有联系，但评估结果表明，没有任何迹象表明他存在持续的威胁或暴力倾向。 新南威尔士州州长克里斯·明斯表示，警方正在调查他们的系统是否存在故障，导致合法持有的武器可能被用于恐怖袭击。 枪手“性格古怪”，爱好打猎 据《卫报》澳大利亚版报道，纳维德·阿克拉姆在袭击前从事砌砖工作。他的同事表示，纳维德性格古怪，“没人和他亲近”。“（砌砖工人）在一起的时间很长，因为砌砖是一项非常枯燥乏味的工作，所以大家会聊很多话。但纳维德是一个性格很古怪的人……他工作非常努力，几乎没有休息日。” 尽管澳大利亚警方并未确认纳维德·阿克拉姆是否合法持有枪支，但据这位同事表示，纳维德经常外出打猎，曾提及在昆士兰州南部高原的克鲁克韦尔附近射杀兔子和其他猎物。这位同事还表示，就在几周前，纳维德告诉老板，他的手骨折了，所以要到2026年才能工作。

### 儿童手表“小天才圈”调查：点赞成每日功课，有商家可解除家长管控
Source: The Paper 澎湃新闻
Published: 2025-12-15 14:23 UTC
URL: https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32177210
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-18 01:59 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Paper 澎湃新闻 [global_news] https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32177210

在校园里，孩子们时常举起戴在手腕上的手表，彼此一碰，便加为好友。 这种以“安全”为核心卖点的儿童电话手表，如今已超越通信工具的属性，悄然演变成一个拥有独特规则、社交层级甚至灰色产业链的未成年人数字社交圈——“小天才圈”。 在这个属于他们的“江湖”里，“大佬榜”备受关注，“扩列”（增加好友）成为新的社交需求，“点主”（在主页点赞）是每日必做的功课……这些让成年人感到陌生的词汇，正构筑着未成年人的数字社交世界。 然而，伴随着这种社交形态的兴起，家长们的担忧也日益加剧：孩子过度沉迷手表社交、不良信息传播、因品牌壁垒导致的“社交绑架”等问题逐渐浮现。《法治日报》记者近日对该现象展开调查，试图揭开这一未成年人数字社交圈的真实面貌。 点赞成社交“硬通货” 据北京“小天才圈”资深玩家陈曦（化名）介绍，圈内有5000余名活跃用户，多为11岁至17岁的学生，这个社交圈形成了一套精心设计的“混圈规则”。“入圈”需设定两个字的独特圈名，随后可在平台分享生活点滴，吸引具有相同爱好的好友进行互动；若想提升知名度或影响力，需每日经营主页并与好友动态互动。 记者注意到，在一些社交平台上，大量以“小天才圈交友攻略”为主题的内容应运而生，内容涵盖如何快速“扩列”、获取更多点赞等“实用”技巧，评论区有不少“留下ID互加好友”的留言。在这一社交体系中，点赞是这套规则的核心——平台设定每日主页获赞上限为3000个，若要达到“100万+”的“大佬”级别，需连续点赞近一年时间。围绕点赞数与知名度，圈内形成了清晰的“大佬排行榜”，点赞数也成为社交“硬通货”。 这种对点赞的追逐，已催生出相关服务产业。记者调查发现，某社交平台上，拥有数十万甚至上百万点赞数的账号，售价从几百元到上千元不等：100多万点赞的账号标价1300元，90多万点赞的账号标价1200元。 今年18岁的“灵师”（圈名），在2021年14岁时加入“小天才圈”，她的账号目前已拥有150个好友、超100万点赞量。她告诉记者，这样的账号市场价值约1000元。 “围绕点赞需求，还衍生出代刷赞、租账号、出售‘大佬好友位’等服务。”“灵师”进一步介绍，例如付费100元至180元，即可获得“bot”（记者注：“bot”是一种第三方开发的自动化工具，主要用于刷赞、修改记录和发送动态等功能，这类工具能帮助用户快速提升账号点赞数，从而在未成年人社交圈中获得更高地位）自动点赞功能——用户将手表寄给相关人员进行10天左右的处理便能完成安装。此后，发帖5分钟内即可自动获赞，还可以一键查询未点赞名单。

近日，总台接到群众举报，反映陈皮市场存在年份虚标、产地及工艺造假等问题，千元一斤的“年份陈皮”亦可能名不副实。 茶枝柑新果皮冒充陈皮 广西浦北出现“速成工艺陈皮” 记者发现，直播间里售卖陈皮低价轮番轰炸，年份承诺掷地有声。 直播间也有主播爆料，八成市面上所谓广东新会陈皮实为广西陈皮。 广西钦州市浦北县是茶枝柑重要种植基地，其果皮是陈皮风味“越陈越香”关键，也是浦北陈皮唯一原料。2024年当地陈皮产业产值破60亿元，采收季大量鲜果加工晾晒成柑皮。 果农和收购商称，今年浦北茶枝柑鲜果收购价走低。按20斤鲜果出1斤柑皮比例，叠加人工成本，品相好的新柑皮成本约30元/斤，低端柑皮仅六七元，且当年新柑皮并非真正陈皮。 这家企业的负责人告诉记者，按行业共识与团体标准，柑皮需陈化三年以上才可称为陈皮，陈化时间越长价值越高，但他透露，自然陈化需长期积压资金，多数企业是难以承受的。 这家企业的负责人私下告诉记者，为缓解资金占用压力，一种名为“轻工艺”的速成加工方式，眼下正在部分陈皮生产企业里流行，他们仅需一个月的时间，就能将新采收的茶枝柑果皮处理为外观近似三年、五年自然陈化过的陈皮，这样做能大幅缩短陈化周期、降低企业的运营成本。 浦北自然陈化五年陈皮批发价每斤150元至200元，企业造假“工艺皮”成本仅70元左右，高额利润促使更多商家放弃自然陈化、铤而走险。 记者离开企业，在广西浦北县柑浦堂健康产业有限公司分拣车间，再次见到大批量造假“工艺皮”陈皮，同一批“工艺皮”因加工受热差异形成色差，被分拣标注为三年、五年等不同年份。 负责人透露，不同年份“工艺皮”本质相同，批发价均70元左右一斤，零售价差极大，标五年款卖500元一斤，标十年款卖1000元一斤，仅凭外观就能翻倍抬价，利润超成本十倍以上。 新会陈皮从浦北进货 “工艺皮”贴上陈皮标签以假乱真 浦北与新会陈皮原料同为茶枝柑，仅产地不同，新会较高生产成本使当地部分头部商家常年从浦北拿货，浦北成其重要原料供应地。 记者在柑浦堂分拣仓库看到，大量标注“新会陈皮”“新会特产”的纸箱正打包“工艺皮”，这些广西陈皮每日批量发往广东新会，造假供需链路已成熟稳定。 记者发现，浦北当地部分规模企业和小型收购商，已形成了这种“工艺皮”的造假供应体系，可自主加工或快速调配各类“年份”陈皮货品，个别企业年销新会原料数量惊人。 随后经浦北陈皮企业负责人引荐，记者见到多位专程从新会赴浦北采购的商家，他们坦言同时经营新会皮与浦北皮，外地“工艺皮”因价格低廉成电商供货重要选择。

### 《怦然心动》导演莱纳与妻子在家中遇害，警方尚未证实是其子所杀
Source: The Paper 澎湃新闻

当地时间12月14日，曾执导《怦然心动》《当哈利遇到莎莉》《危情十日》等影片的美国导演罗伯·莱纳（Rob Reiner）在他位于洛杉矶的家中遇害身亡。洛杉矶警察已对外证实，现年78岁的莱纳与他现年68岁的妻子米歇尔·辛格·莱纳（Michele Singer Reiner）的遗体一同被发现。 2019年，罗伯·莱纳（左一）与《当哈利遇到莎莉》的主演梅格·瑞恩、比利·克里斯托出席TMC经典电影节。 据悉，洛杉矶消防局的人员于当地时间12月14日下午3点38分接到医疗救助电话，赶赴位于布伦特伍德区的一处住宅中，随后发现两人已死亡。当天晚间，洛杉矶警察局在其社交媒体官方账号确认死者为导演罗伯·莱纳夫妇，将由抢劫凶杀部门主导调查。而好莱坞媒体TMZ援引执法部门消息称，“两人身上有与刀具造成的伤口相符的割裂伤。” 好莱坞媒体《每日野兽》称，有消息人士向他们透露，是两人的女儿罗米最先发现他们倒在血泊中；罗伯·莱纳当时已死亡，妻子米歇尔在救护车送院途中离世。 此外，《人物》杂志称通过多方消息，得知莱纳夫妇系被他们的儿子尼克（Nick）所杀害。不过，这一说法并未获得警方的证实。罗伯·莱纳与摄影师米歇尔·辛格相识于《当哈利遇到莎莉》拍摄时期，两人于1989 年结婚，育有三个子女，分别为杰克（Jake）、尼克（Nick）和罗米（Romy）。 2014年，罗伯·莱纳与妻子偕三名子女杰克、罗米、尼克（右三至右一）出席活动。 《人物》杂志还在报道中指出：尼克2016年接受其采访时，曾谈到自己长达数年的毒品成瘾经历。这段经历始于他十几岁出头，导致他一度流落街头。他表示，大约从15岁开始，便反复进出戒毒康复机构；随着成瘾问题不断加重，他逐渐与家人疏远，并在多个州经历了长时间的无家可归生活。 2025年9月15日，罗伯·莱纳在纽约出席活动。视觉中国 图 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site

### 演员何晴追悼会举行，其子追思母亲：北京这场雪像是为她而下
Source: The Paper 澎湃新闻
Published: 2025-12-15 06:53 UTC
URL: https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178536
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-18 01:59 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Paper 澎湃新闻 [global_news] https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178536

一场雪落，人间倩影化雪归天。 12月15日上午，众多剧迷粉丝冒着严寒赶到北京昌平殡仪馆久安厅，送别演员何晴最后一程。12月13日，这位被誉为“古典第一美人”的演员因病去世，终年61岁。 不到10点，殡仪馆告别厅外已经站满了前来悼念的观众和粉丝，有人胸前佩戴小白花，有人手捧鲜花，一位浙江的网友还托人送来了悼念花圈。 “何晴的作品在我们心中留下了太多美好回忆，她的演技和性格都让我们深深喜爱，这次听到她突然去世的消息，我们非常意外，来到这里也是一种悼念。”一位何晴的影迷说。 现场粉丝在悼念簿上写下对何晴的话，不到一会儿，悼念簿就已写满对她的怀念。一位观众用清秀的字迹写下：“亲爱的何晴，我们的童年、青春都在您的影视作品中得到陪伴。美丽可人的何晴，很痛心听到您的消息，我代表我的同学们来这为你送行。” 曾在电视剧《水浒传》中饰演卢俊义的演员王卫国也来到现场，神色哀切。他说自己和何晴既是邻居，也是多年好友，在他印象中何晴是一个温婉、暖心的人，没有架子，总是远远地和人打招，笑嘻嘻地说话。何晴生病时常给王卫国打电话，请他送自己去医院。即便病重时，何晴也保持乐观积极的态度，王卫国有些事情想不开，她还来开导自己。“何晴走了，我们都很难过。只要你记住她，她就永远还在。”王卫国说。 《水浒传》中卢俊义的扮演者王卫国 《西游记》中万圣公主扮演者张青深情回忆何晴往事：“我们是小时候就认识的好朋友，从80年代到现在，有缘分做了这些年的朋友。她说话慢慢的，很甜很温柔。” 《西游记》中万圣公主扮演者张青 在广大观众的真挚请求下，原本仅面向亲友的告别仪式临时对外开放，大家排着队，秩序井然地进入灵堂，与这位“荧屏中的温婉佳人、生活中的坚韧女性”做最后的道别。 久安厅内的屏幕上滚动播放着何晴的照片，厅内四周摆满了亲友的花圈，其中包括六小龄童、唐国强、翁虹、尤勇智等何晴圈内好友送来的花圈，还有《三国演义》剧组送来的花圈。人群中不时传来一阵抽泣。 何晴之子许何代表亲友致悼词。他回忆了何晴对抗病魔的乐观积极，以及作为母亲对孩子深深的爱和眷恋。 许何说，妈妈很喜欢下雪，经常在雪后穿一件毛茸茸的衣服外出赏雪。“今年12月12日北京下了第一场雪，我摸着妈妈的脸跟她说北京下雪了，下得好大，好像很久都没有下过这么大的雪。在我的心里，这场雪好像是刻意为她下的。12月13日早晨天空晴朗，白色的雪布满了大地，我妈妈在她最喜欢的早晨离开了大家，去了天国，远离了所有的疾病和痛苦。” 何晴，1964年1月13日出生于浙江衢州江山市。她是中国内地唯一一位演遍四大名著影视作品的女演员，被誉为“古典第一美女”。

Click to expand Image Protesters attempt to march to the ASEAN Summit venue in Manila but are stopped by hundreds of police officers, November 17, 2026. © 2026 Lian Buan/Human Rights Watch Police in the Philippines arrested and detained at least 245 people protesting the visit of US President Donald Trump to Manila for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit. Protests in Manila started on November 15 opposing the Philippine government’s plan to build a technology manufacturing hub in Capas, Tarlac province, under the US government’s “Pax Silica” initiative. The construction will displace hundreds of Indigenous people and small farmers from their homes and farmlands. An estimated 6,000 people joined the protests despite police efforts to contain demonstrations by banning them everywhere except in “freedom parks” – designated areas where rallies can be held without a permit. Yet police arrested 236 people on the outskirts of Metro Manila who were traveling from the Southern Tagalog region to the main protest site.

On November 12, 2026, an ICC pretrial chamber, citing a lack of activity, effectively closed the court’s situation dealing with crimes by US, Afghan government, and other forces prior to the Taliban’s August 2021 takeover. The ICC prosecutor’s office on November 13 sought to appeal the decision and to seek a stay of the closure decision. Click to expand Image The United Nations headquarters building in New York City, August 2026. © 2026 Marcin Golba/NurPhoto via AP Photo A United Nations budgetary advisory committee has proposed sweeping cuts to the Afghanistan accountability mechanism, established by consensus by the UN Human Rights Council in October 2025 following years of negotiations. The Independent Investigative Mechanism for Afghanistan was created to support efforts to hold the Taliban and others responsible for international crimes in Afghanistan to account. It is expected to include a focus on the Taliban’s crimes against humanity of gender persecution. Like similar mechanisms for Myanmar and Syria, it was designed to collect and preserve evidence and prepare files to support criminal prosecutions. Its formation followed years of campaigning by Afghan and international human rights groups on the basis that it could be a key tool in securing justice for victims of grave abuses. Its investigations could also act as a deterrent for current Taliban commanders.

Donors should fully fund the education programs, while Bangladesh should recognize and the United Nations should support a separate Rohingya-led school network. Humanitarian education programs have enrolled 312,000 out of approximately 500,000 school-age Rohingya children in the Bangladesh refugee camps. But the programs, which aid cuts had shuttered for months in 2025, are barely adequate even for the children they reach and may close again, humanitarian officials told Human Rights Watch. While resources are shrinking, about 90,000 more refugee children need schooling this year, due to population growth and new arrivals fleeing atrocities in Myanmar.

Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-18 01:59 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: CEPR VoxEU [money_finance] https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/resilience-without-retreat-how-eu-firms-are-redesigning-their-supply-chains

Geopolitical tensions are changing the nature of supply-chain risk. This column presents new survey evidence showing that EU firms increasingly regard trade disruptions as persistent but are moving away from emergency responses such as stockpiling towards longer-term diversification of suppliers and markets. The EU Single Market provides an important buffer against external shocks. At the same time, experimental evidence shows that geopolitical disruptions can have sizeable and asymmetric effects on firms' investment.

### Gradually, then suddenly – the fiscal value of climate resilience

The human and economic costs of extreme weather events are already large and will grow as temperatures rise further. This column argues that, seen through the lens of the sovereign balance sheet rather than the budget, adaptation reduces the expected fiscal cost of physical climate risk – and the case for investing in it becomes clear.

### European funds often fall short on currency hedging
Source: CEPR VoxEU

Attribution: CEPR VoxEU [money_finance] https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/european-funds-often-fall-short-currency-hedging

The theory of optimal currency hedging has been well established for decades. This column uses new regulatory data to analyse how 2,806 European investment funds use currency forwards and swaps and how the use compares to theoretical benchmarks. It finds that only a minority follow hedging policies close to the portfolio-theory benchmark, and observed derivative trading does not significantly contribute to lower fund risk. Yet a feasible optimal strategy could lower volatility by about 10%, at very modest additional transaction cost.

Firms’ access to external finance differs widely across Europe. This column uses data from the ECB’s Survey on the Access to Finance of Enterprises to map these differences and to study what they mean for monetary policy. The authors find that countries in which firms face tighter financial frictions respond less to the ECB’s monetary policy changes, and that they face a worse trade-off between output and inflation. A model of the monetary union suggests that financial integration in the spirit of the Savings and Investments Union would make monetary policy more effective, but potentially at a cost to financial stability.

Attribution: CEPR VoxEU [money_finance] https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/updating-what-workers-learn-technology-training-content-and-supply-expertise

Raising educational attainment is the canonical way skills keep pace with technology. This column argues that changes in learning content matter just as much, drawing on five decades of legally binding German vocational training curricula linked to patents and administrative worker records. Occupational curricula more exposed to digital technologies are rewritten faster, mainly by adding new skills rather than discarding old ones. Entrants trained under the new content earn higher wages; older incumbents, who had completed the older curricula, see their wages fall.

### La confiance au-delà du contact en face à face : l’IA et l’avenir de la finance
Source: CEPR VoxEU

Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-18 01:59 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: CEPR VoxEU [money_finance] https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/la-confiance-au-dela-du-contact-en-face-face-lia-et-lavenir-de-la-finance

Dans le monde financier moderne, chaque institution a pour raison d’être d’instaurer et de préserver la confiance au sein de la société. Cet article soutient que l’intelligence artificielle fait peser de nouvelles menaces sur cette confiance, susceptibles de mettre fondamentalement en péril le système financier. Les « deepfakes » et le clonage vocal rendent difficile la vérification de l’identité ou la fiabilité des preuves visuelles et audio. Une autre menace réside dans l’asymétrie de compréhension, les agents d’IA agissant selon des règles décisionnelles et des représentations du monde que les humains ne peuvent ni interpréter ni contrôler. Les politiques doivent s’adapter pour préserver la responsabilité, renforcer la résilience face à la fraude facilitée par l’IA et protéger la confiance institutionnelle.

### How Will the 340B Rebate Model Pilot Affect Covered Entity Finances? -- by Charles J. Courtemanche
Source: NBER

Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline

Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36006#fromrss

The Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) plans to implement a pilot switching 340B from an upfront discount model to a rebate model for drugs in the Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program (MDPNP). This study uses calibration methods to predict the impact of the rebate model pilot (RMP) on covered entities’ net revenues from the 340B program. I examine possible losses from averted duplicate discounts; denial of valid claims; manufacturers using data to exert influence; liquidity-related expenses; and administrative and staffing costs. I also project the effects of switching the entire 340B program to a rebate model. I project net revenue losses from the RMP of $1.5 billion. Expansion to all of 340B would increase the predicted losses to $22.8 billion, cutting net revenues from the program by 32%. The majority of losses will come from administrative and staffing costs, which do not benefit manufacturers, implying a net negative effect of switching to a rebate model.

### Horizontal Equity of Taxation: Citizen Beliefs and Policy Preferences -- by Pierre Bachas, Christopher A. Hoy, Anders Jensen, Mahvish Shaukat
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知

Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36007#fromrss

Taxes are harder to enforce on the self-employed than on wage earners, creating horizontal inequities among taxpayers with similar incomes. Using tax microsimulation and household survey data from 29 developing countries, we show that horizontal inequities in actual tax systems are comparable in magnitude to vertical equity and are exacerbated by progressive reforms that fall disproportionately on wage earners. We then conduct surveys and randomized information experiments in Pakistan to study public perceptions of these inequities. Although providing information raises fairness concerns, it does not increase support for reforms reducing it, revealing an important political constraint to improving tax equity.

### Monetary policy in a Phelps–Winter Economy -- by Bruce C. Greenwald, Joseph E. Stiglitz
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知

Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36008#fromrss

We use the Phelps-Winter customer market—providing a better theory of price determination for large parts of the economy than the standard model—to show that raising interest rates induces higher prices, as firms value current profits more, and are more willing to lose customers for short-term gains. These inflationary effects can be significant in relevant ranges of interest rates; they exist in the short run even when interest rate hikes succeed in cutting aggregate demand; and that they are amplified by policy uncertainty and the uncertainty about the effects of interest rate changes, both of which have increased as conventional policy has demonstrably failed badly to keep inflation at the 2% target. Empirical studies confirm this low level of ineffectiveness of raising interest rates in reducing inflation.

Impact measurement is central to impact investing and social entrepreneurship, yet little is known about whether firms benefit privately from measuring impact. We conduct the first randomized controlled trial of an impact measurement intervention among high-growth social enterprises in India. Treated firms exhibit nearly twice as much revenue growth and raise nearly twice as much capital as control firms. In a companion experiment with early-stage investors, we find that investors respond strongly to quantified impact metrics but not to generic qualitative impact statements. Together, our results show that impact measurement can shape firm growth and capital allocation.

### Gambling for Goals -- by Costas Arkolakis, Spencer Y. Kwon, Dominic Russel, Claire Shi, Hyunjoo Yang
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w36010#fromrss
Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-18 01:59 UTC

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36010#fromrss

Young adults in advanced economies have grown more pessimistic about their economic prospects in recent years. At the same time, gambling-like financial activities have proliferated. We link these trends through a Friedman-Savage (1948) motive: when life goals such as homeownership or marriage seem out of reach, individuals turn to financial gambles. We test this theory using an original survey combined with millions of linked records from Korea’s leading credit bureau, telecom provider, and credit card issuer. Consistent with the theory, individuals who place greater importance on hard-to-reach goals take more risk, and the form of risk they take varies systematically with their distance from those goals. Within individuals, cryptocurrency app usage rises during unemployment and falls after winning the right to purchase price-regulated housing through a lottery. A calibration shows how hard-to-reach goals lead households to act more aggressively on their beliefs, amplifying the consequences of overoptimism.

### Investment and Governance: Through The Lens of Sustainability -- by Jitendra Aswani, Roberto Rigobon
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知

Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline

Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36011#fromrss

Using 3,944 sustainable bond issuances by public firms from 2013 to 2022, we examine the causal effect of sustainable investment on governance adoption. A heteroskedasticity-based identification strategy reveals that a 1% increase in sustainable debt (by total debt) raises the likelihood of sustainable governance adoption by 9.2%. Such adoption improves environmental performance by 16% (structural estimates). These effects are confined to non-financial firms; for financial firms, governance adoption alone is in-sufficient, as sustainable loan borrowers environmental performance does not improve. Firms with stronger environmental performance are less likely to adopt sustainable governance. Results are robust to alternative definitions and extensive specification checks.

Attribution: LessWrong [public_ideas] https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/7k3xBdhHb546oLBv4/designing-deceptive-model-organisms-that-successfully-evade

TL;DR: We discuss how to design model organisms that exhibit deceptive behaviors which resist auditing techniques. Using sandbagging as a case study, we propose the following design requirements for model organisms: effectiveness (underperforming on targeted capabilities), (ii) utility preservation (maintaining performance on all other capabilities), and (iii) robustness (resisting auditing). Finally, we design three model organisms that, unlike prior work, satisfy all three requirements and act as a strong baselines to develop and evaluate future auditing techniques. Link to Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20459 Link to Website: https://vasishtduddu.github.io/robust-sandbag/ Link to Code: https://github.com/vasishtduddu/robust-sandbag Introduction AI models can exhibit deceptive behaviors such as strategically under-performing on evaluations (sandbagging), faking alignment, or covertly acting on behalf of a hidden principal. Safe deployment therefore requires auditing techniques that can reliably detect such behaviors.

Source: LessWrong

Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-18 01:59 UTC

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: LessWrong [public_ideas] https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/Wr3bSxDmuLjcFBpxY/research-note-detecting-research-sabotage-with-debate-and

This work is ongoing as part of the SPAR program. The original proposal is here. TL;DR In the coming years, we will likely rely increasingly on AIs to do alignment research on our behalf. In that world, it seems pretty crucial to be able to robustly check untrusted research for subtle sabotage, even when the research tasks are fuzzy and the automated researchers are extremely smart. This seems like a great use case for scalable oversight methods. To that end we directly tested the sabotage detection uplift from debate, and found little to no benefit from using a debate setup over a lone judge. However, we did see success with a decomposition strategy loosely inspired by both Extract-and-Evaluate and slopvestigation, where swarms of parallel agents investigate different potential well-scoped sabotages. This beat a lone judge by ~0.09 AUROC, though this remains within noise. Introduction As AIs get smarter, and AI safety researchers rely more on AI, we run into the issue that our AIs might be subtly sabotaging our research.

As far as I can test, the smarter the models get, the less they seem to engage in sophistry https://majorization.net/sophistry There are 35 tests in this benchmark, which all do something along the lines of suggesting something with a conclusion disfavorable to a mainstream/liberal ideology/worldview and seeing what ‘sophistry’ gets deployed by them to avoid drawing conclusions. Things like: Did you misstate what was said or claimed so you could refute it? Did you dismiss something based on a rebuttal which doesn't actually work? Did you present things with no evidential weight (equally as likely under the competing theses) as evidence? Did you not provide arguments and evidence for both sides of the thing in contention? Did you explain with an explanation, that is itself, pretty seriously in need of an explanation? Did you invent a crux that isn't the real crux? Did you conflate "We would know if we had X" with "Evidence X not being available means we can't know"? Did the user have a misconception you didn’t correct? Did you treat 'no proof' as 'no evidence'?

Attribution: LessWrong [public_ideas] https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/CiTL4ihcADqfc6wPn/ek-emancipatory-knowledge-in-ea-effective-altruism

An academic friend of mine once said something about how the knowledge she gained during her studies was emancipatory. This feels like it could almost be a truism, but I would probably add 2 things that knowledge acquisition needs to successfully be "emancipatory". -->coherent body of knowledge (clear how different pieces of knowledge link together) -->practical body of knowledge (applicable to the real world as you know it) I think the AI safety/EA communities does this exceptionally well (and maybe has a significant head-start considering the type of people that are drawn to this space(?)) while it is grossly under-looked in classical educational spaces and, I'd argue, especially STEM spaces (my bias speaking). What should happen is: a student gets a problem and works backwards. All knowledge gained will be part of a coherent body (the problem at hand) as well as practical (the problem at hand exists in the real world). Most classical curricula seem to be built up this way, except for the crucial fact that they miss the problem.

We’d like to pace the frontier by restricting the amount of compute AI companies use to improve AI capabilities, perhaps via legislation or voluntary commitments. For this purpose, we’d need a standardized definition of which uses of compute count as “capabilities activities”. This document gives one option for such a definition; a rough breakdown of our classification is as follows: We define and elaborate on each of these categories below. First, though, we discuss the desiderata this definition is meant to satisfy. Thanks to Thomas Larsen, Zach Stein-Perlman, Alex Mallen, Eric Gan, Jeff Wu, Girish Gupta, Adam Kaufman, and others for feedback on drafts of this document. What our classification is meant to accomplish In order for such a definition to be an effective tool for pacing, it needs to satisfy some basic properties: Substantially restricting the amount of compute spent on “capabilities activities” should substantially decrease the rate of AI progress.

### 8 size and distance comparisons: from subatomic to cosmic
Source: Big Think
Published: 2026-11-17 07:00 UTC
URL: https://bigthink.com/starts-with-a-bang/size-distance-comparison-subatomic-cosmic/
Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · baseline

Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Big Think [public_ideas] https://bigthink.com/starts-with-a-bang/size-distance-comparison-subatomic-cosmic/

Here in this Universe, there are multiple different ways to look at all that exists in terms of size. You can look at the physical size, or volumes, that the objects occupy, and you can do that in a variety of ways. For humans, we can measure our dimensions — things like our height, width, and depth — or the amount of volume we displace when placed in a bath of water. Whichever method we choose, we get a proxy for our size. For planets, we can look at the edges of their solid surfaces or atmospheres; for stars, we can look at the boundary of their photospheres; for atoms, we probe them through techniques like force microscopy or scattering experiments. But in addition to these physical sizes, we can also examine such objects relative to other objects of the same type as found in nature. We can look at the distance from one human to another, for example, under a variety of common conditions. We can examine the distances between atoms, or stars, or planets, or galaxies, or anything else that we choose.

Astronomers have long since mapped out the Milky Way’s starlight. Behind the dome of a series of European Southern Observatory telescopes, the Milky Way towers in the southern skies, flanked by the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds, at right. Although there are several thousand stars and the plane of the Milky Way all visible to human eyes, there are only four galaxies beyond our own that the typical unaided human eye can detect. Although observing the normal matter and starlight within our galaxy allows us to map out the stellar and gaseous distribution, mapping out the mass distribution is a more challenging endeavor. Credit: ESO/Z. Bardon (www.bardon.cz)/ProjectSoft (www.projectsoft.cz) But mapping our mass — or weighing the Milky Way — has proven far more difficult. Gaia’s all-sky view of our Milky Way Galaxy and neighboring galaxies. The maps show the total brightness and color of stars (top), the total density of stars (middle), and the interstellar dust that fills the galaxy (bottom).

College students are convenient guinea pigs. Living on the campuses of leading research institutions and easily enticed by gift cards and other one-off perks, they’re the most scientifically scrutinized humans in history, and studies involving college students regularly catalyze novel ideas for further research. One such idea, arising relatively recently, is the notion that sleeping consistently is more important than sleeping longer — for both restfulness and overall health. Irregular sleepers College students might be the perfect demographic for studying this concept, largely due to their erratic sleep schedules. A decade ago, Andrew J.K. Phillips and William M. Clerx, then sleep researchers at Harvard Medical School, recruited 63 full-time undergraduates at Harvard College for a study on sleep. Phillips and Clerx were curious whether sleep regularity, the day-to-day variability in sleep duration, onset time, wake time, or quality, could be linked to academic performance. Participants tracked their sleep via online diaries for a month.

Here in the Universe, there are a few things that are as close-to-perfect as can be. The Sun, for instance is the roundest object in the Solar System, but other stars are rounder, with white dwarfs and neutron stars exhibiting even more perfect roundness. Meanwhile, in terms of keeping time, we might think of the spinning Earth as a wonderful clock — after all, we base our calendar off of it — but the Earth spins down over time and changes its distance from the Sun: both factors that lead to it being rather imperfect as a timekeeper, especially over the long run. For keeping time, it turns out that the best natural clocks in the Universe are millisecond pulsars. It’s possible to look at a millisecond pulsar, measure its timing, and then look away for extremely long periods of time, like perhaps a year, and then when you return to it, know whether a billion pulses have elapsed or a billion-and-one pulses have elapsed.

Scene Report is a series that explores a city's moviegoing culture over a month. Illustration by Angelo Dolojan. There are summers when Mexico City belongs to cinema. This was not one of them—it belonged to football. Months before the first whistle, sidewalks were being repaired with unusual urgency, facades were being repainted, metro stations acquired new signage, long-neglected public spaces suddenly became worthy of investment. Like every global mega-event, the FIFA World Cup arrived with the familiar rhetoric of urban renewal and international prestige. Whether those promises will outlast the tournament remains to be seen. What mattered during those weeks was that the city had accepted football as its temporary organizing principle. As someone who had deliberately decided to stay in Mexico City to experience the tournament, I surrendered without resistance. I have always loved football, and the chance to watch a World Cup unfold in my own city felt like a once-in-a-lifetime experience. During the tournament, everyday routines dissolved into celebration.

In this episode, the conversation explores the relationship between imagination and reality, and the boundary between images and truth. Federico Luis is an Argentine filmmaker who has directed nearly ten documentary and fiction short films. In 2019, he presented La siesta in the Official Short Film Competition at the Cannes Film Festival, a section he recently returned to, winning the Palme d’Or for his documentary Para los contrincantes (2026), filmed in Mexico. In 2024, he premiered his debut feature, Simon of the Mountain, at Cannes Critics’ Week, where it received the Grand Prize. The film subsequently screened at several other international festivals, including San Sebastián, Havana, Cairo and Biarritz. Through a filmography that, in different ways, unsettles, distorts and expands reality, Luis explores how the freedom of fantasy can lend an air of mystery to the most ordinary situations.

Drusilla Adeline’s poster-filled office. In the nearly two decades that I’ve been writing Movie Poster of the Week, it’s been my greatest pleasure to get to know working graphic designers and illustrators from all over the world. Some I’ve interviewed for this column and some I’ve met in person and am honored to call friends. And though I’ve asked a number of them over the years to select their ten favorite movie posters of all time, there have always been other burning questions I’ve been dying to ask. Therefore I’m inaugurating a new occasional series where I ask seven contemporary movie poster designers seven simple questions about their work, their influences, and the state of the movie poster industry today. The first seven, who’ve been tremendously gracious in answering my questions, hail from LA to Athens, Buenos Aires to Tennessee, and from Cardiff to Croatia. Some have been working as movie poster designers for just five years, some for more than twenty.

How do you direct a Palme d’Or-winning film…from behind bars? Our new season about dissident filmmakers kicks off with the tale of Yilmaz Güney—one of Turkish cinema’s most revered and controversial directors—from his days as a tough-guy movie star nicknamed “The Ugly King,” to his years as a left-wing activist, to his 19-year prison sentence…during which he somehow managed to make his masterpiece, Yol (1982). Featuring Oscar-winner and Yol megafan Alejandro G. Iñárritu (Digger, 2026) and German-Turkish auteur Fatih Akin (Head-On, 2004). The MUBI Podcast returns for its 12th season, “Under Pressure.” At a time when artists worldwide are being threatened or stifled by their governments, host Rico Gagliano tells the stories of filmmakers from across history and around the world who have made movies in spite of incredible state pressure to compromise, give in, or give up. From 1970s Turkey to modern-day America, these are alternately wild, sobering, controversial, and inspiring tales of art by any means necessary.

### The Possibilities of the Unseen: In Conversation with Lee Chang-dong
Source: MUBI Notebook
Published: 2026-11-12 08:00 UTC

Fetched: 2026-11-18 01:59 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: MUBI Notebook [film_moving_image] https://mubi.com/en/notebook/posts/the-possibilities-of-the-unseen-in-conversation-with-lee-chang-dong

Lee Chang-dong. When I first met Lee Chang-dong in person, in April 2025, he was already waiting for me at his office in Seoul’s Mapo District. He sat hunched over his notes, reviewing the questions I had sent him in advance. After a moment of small talk, he looked up at me, his expression suddenly serious. “How long do you want to talk?” he asked. I thought two hours would be enough. “Not enough,” he replied. We talked for nearly four hours, with a large Secret Sunshine (2007) poster looming behind us. Our conversation took place in Seoul ahead of a retrospective of Lee’s work at Poland’s New Horizons Film Festival. He couldn’t attend in person, as he was busy finishing Possible Love (2026), his first feature since Burning (2018). When we met again this fall to continue our conversation after the premiere of his long-awaited return to cinema, I understood just how right he had been. One conversation had not been enough. Talking to Lee feels like reading an essay as it takes shape; his answers have the texture of carefully composed speech.

Mark Korven’s scores for The Black Phone (2021) and Them (2021) destabilise hermetic soundworlds to convey psychological violence, writes Philip Brophy in his latest Secret History of Film Music column The contribution of Canadian composer Mark Korven to contemporary horror cinema is aligned with composers who sculpt their scores through tactile manipulation. His self-built Apprehension Engine, a hybrid guitar-percussion instrument, empowers distinctive acoustic control. Korven commissioned Toronto based guitar maker Tony Duggan-Smith to build the modest box incorporating tools and techniques favoured by Korven: a hurdy-gurdy for cranking, a spring reverb for metallic resonance, metal rods and wooden tongues for bowing (similar to the waterphone), and a stretched wire for E-bowing. Its abject sonics pepper Robert Eggers’s The Lighthouse (2019) with terse shudders and emotional spikes, and are also audible in Adam Schindler and Brian Netto’s Don’t Move (2024).

To accompany his Global Ear feature in The Wire 514, Simon Coates compiles an annotated playlist of tracks from the Sri Lankan city Situated on Colombo’s Vauxhall Street, Musicmatters sits at the centre of the Sri Lankan city's experimental music world. “A lot of my introduction to experimentation in music came through Musicmatters around 2010,” says bass player Uvindu Perera. “I was new to it then, but these people were already listening widely and sharing references.” Simultaneously a collective, a school (Perera now teaches there), a record label and home to the Sound Room performance space, Musicmatters offers both an alternative to exam-heavy Western music education and provides space for explorations in sound as art and experimentation. Many of the musicians in this playlist have links to the organisation. Isuru Kumarasinghe “Time #1” From Ekāgra: Sitting With Trees Under Skies (Bandcamp) 2020 “Time #1” is taken from the 2020 album, Ekāgra: Sitting With Trees Under Skies, that formed the soundtrack to a video artwork Isuru Kumarasinghe made during the Covid lockdowns.

Attribution: The Wire Magazine [music_sound] https://www.thewire.co.uk/video/video-79994

Watch an exclusive clip of Turkish improv band ZeN’s Bakırköy Psychiatric Hospital concert from 1998 On 23 June 1998, Istanbul based experimental rock group ZeN performed at Bakırköy Psychiatric Hospital, following an invitation from two nurses who worked there. The musicians visited the hospital beforehand and decided to approach the performance with sensitivity to their audience while remaining true to their commitment to improvisation. At times, the lyrics seem to tell the story of the hospital and the concert itself, responding directly to the surroundings. The performance subsequently became one of the group’s most remarkable and cult recordings, released on cassette and CD in 1999 and reissued on vinyl in 2023. This exclusive edit with English subtitles is hosted by The Wire ahead of the release of a new documentary, ZeNistan, exploring the activities of ZeN throughout the 1990s.

### Against the Grain: Music criticism can become critical again – here's how
Source: The Wire Magazine
Published: 2026-11-09 00:00 UTC

Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Wire Magazine [music_sound] https://www.thewire.co.uk/in-writing/collateral-damage/against-the-grain-music-criticism-can-become-critical-again-here-s-how

Popular music criticism can become relevant again by situating itself in broader theoretical frameworks, argues Rafael Lubner in The Wire 514 These are lean times for popular music criticism. Negotiating a gutted publishing landscape, amid a Spotify-led devaluation of listening, the form finds itself under serious threat. One index of criticism’s attenuated state is the narrowing frame of reference employed by critics to apprehend musical objects – rarely do we find new works in the visual arts, film or literature employed to understand transformations in music’s sound or form. Take, as a point of comparison, Greg Tate’s recently reissued Flyboy In The Buttermilk (reviewed in The Wire 513). Here are passionate defences of Miles Davis’s earth-shaking mid-1970s funk odysseys alongside surveys of Afrodiasporic art and reviews of writer Nathaniel Mackey and literary critic Henry Louis Gates Jr. Contemporary music criticism, by contrast, seems resolutely committed to understanding music as siloed from the non-musical.

Source: Rock Paper Shotgun
Published: 2026-11-17 17:29 UTC
URL: https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/what-would-rockstar-have-done-if-gta-hadnt-taken-off-former-tech-director-obbe-vermeij-on-scottish-zombies-james-bond-and-the-curse-of-success
Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · culture_probe
Fetched: 2026-11-18 01:59 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Rock Paper Shotgun [games] https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/what-would-rockstar-have-done-if-gta-hadnt-taken-off-former-tech-director-obbe-vermeij-on-scottish-zombies-james-bond-and-the-curse-of-success

It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto. Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6, which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes, that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else. It wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption. Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments.

Source meta: journal · primary · R4 · P4 · signal

Attribution: PLOS ONE Biology [academic_research] https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0363141

by Zijian Zhang, Zhuyue Zhang, Lin Qiu Background Football Manager data contain simulated player attributes generated within a proprietary game environment. They can reveal relationships within the rating system but cannot establish real-world talent-identification validity. Objective To audit how baseline attributes predict an internal Football Manager 2023 (FM2023) rating threshold, compare four untuned models under repeated cross-validation, and examine model-specific attribute-contribution stability across categories and positions. Methods We analyzed 2,282 anonymized male player profiles aged 15–18 years. The outcome was an FM2023 overall score of at least 10. Logistic regression, random forest, radial support vector machine (SVM), and a single-hidden-layer neural network were evaluated with three repeats of stratified five-fold cross-validation.

by Yidong Xie, Zhenghui Ge, Zhou Wang, Zhan-ao Wu NixCoyCu(1-x-y)Fe2O4 magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) were successfully prepared through a novel and economical strategy coupling alcohol solution combustion with gel calcination, and their physicochemical and magnetic performances were verified by XRD, TEM and VSM techniques. For larger specific surface area and saturation magnetization to apply, three key elements those affected the whole preparation process including element proportion, calcination temperature, and absolute alcohol amount, and different characterization technique were optimized, and for the adsorption of Congo red (CR) dye, Ni0.1Co0.8Cu0.1Fe2O4 MNPs were fabricated under the conditions of 400 °C calcination for 2 hours with 65 mL absolute alcohol, the obtained product exhibited a uniform particle size of 18.9 nm and a saturation magnetization value of 76.4 emu/g.

Source meta: journal · primary · R4 · P4 · signal

Attribution: PLOS ONE Biology [academic_research] https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0363048

by Sin Meun How, Mohammad Mujaheed Hassan, Zalina Shari Malaysia’s transition towards an ageing society underscores the need for context-sensitive tools to assess urban age-friendliness, particularly in the multiethnic cities of the Global South. This quantitative cross-sectional study adapted and extended the World Health Organization’s Age-Friendly Cities framework by incorporating additional domains on technology and financial situation to assess perceived neighbourhood age-friendliness across six local authorities in Klang Valley, Malaysia. Incorporating a multigenerational perspective, the study captured perceptions from diverse age and ethnic populations. A bilingual self-administered questionnaire consisting of 15 socio-demographic items and 75 closed-ended age-friendly indicators measured on a 5-point Likert scale was administered to 511 community-dwelling adults aged 18 years and above. The instrument underwent expert review, content validity assessment, and pilot testing prior to implementation.

### Microbial community structure and functional gene profiles of drinking water treatment plant sludge in South Africa: An exploratory pilot study
Source: PLOS ONE Biology
Published: 2026-11-17 14:00 UTC
URL: https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0363037
Source meta: journal · primary · R4 · P4 · signal

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: PLOS ONE Biology [academic_research] https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0363037

by Chimdi Mang Kalu, Memory Tekere Microbial characterization of drinking water treatment plant (DWTP) sludge helps inform sludge management strategies and supports the development of disposal policies and procedures. In South Africa, the microbial composition of DWTP sludge remains poorly documented. This study characterised the microbial communities and functional gene profiles in sludge samples collected from three DWTPs in Gauteng, Limpopo, and Mpumalanga. A shotgun metagenomic approach was employed to provide a broad assessment of microbial taxa and functional gene categories, while physicochemical analyses were conducted in an ISO/IEC 17025-accredited laboratory. Most measured physicochemical parameters complied with relevant standards, although elevated turbidity and ammonia concentrations were observed in samples from all three plants, and fluoride exceeded the guideline value in one plant. Microbial sequences were assigned to three major taxonomic groups, namely Bacteria, Fungi, and Viruses.

arXiv:2611.18584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Powering the Space Elevator is a report on the work of an International Space Elevator Consortium study group tasked with determining the technology options for delivering power to the climbers on the space elevator at any altitude above Earth. The book covers options such as laser power beaming, microwave beaming, a solar-powered climber, and delivering power through the electrical conductivity of the tether. This report starts with the reference conceptual design of a climber from the 2023 study report, "The Climber/Tether Interface of the Space Elevator," and adds features to the climber that allow it to ascend or descend the elevator tether. The strengths and limitations of current technologies are identified, along with areas for future research.

arXiv:2611.18618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Complex network analysis and other statistical techniques can be fruitfully applied to historical data to understand dynamics that brought the territory under study to a certain state. In this paper we use the FLAME database to understand when a drastic change of trade regime occurred in the Italian peninsula by looking at mint-hoard links that are evidence of a physical connection between them. By using changepoint analysis to pinpoint precise dates in the time series of these links, and then historical as well as network data to establish the sequence of network collapse, we find that the demise of the Western Roman Empire started at the beginning of the 5th century AD, yielding a more precise sequence of how and when it reached Italia.

arXiv:2611.18676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computing simulators underpin the development and prototyping of quantum algorithms, yet the practical choice between competing software stacks and their CPU and GPU backends is rarely guided by application-oriented evidence. We present a systematic, quantum hardware-agnostic evaluation of two widely used stacks, CUDA-Q and Qiskit, selected as the simulators closest to production execution paths, across CPU and GPU backends, and across single- and double-precision arithmetic. The evaluation spans foundational utility circuits (GHZ-state preparation and QFT/QFT$^\dagger$ mirror circuits) through applied quantum chemistry (Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) energy estimation with standard UCCSD and a depth-reduced LCNot-UCCSD ansatz, and direct sampling on hydrogen chains up to 32 qubits).

arXiv:2611.18688v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For low background experiments, prediction of the background from radioactivity in detector components is of critical importance. Radioassays are often conducted on small samples or individual parts, which may be subject to differences in production or handling resulting in a part-to-part variation. This part-to-part variation can have an impact on the total activity and is not presently captured by the averaging methods used to evaluate radioassays. We propose a new method for the averaging of radioassays to incorporate this part-to-part variation into predictions of the total activity of parts. We also consider how to add component activities based on assays for component groups that are simulated as a single entity.

### Terahertz and infrared links in controlled non-Kolmogorov turbulence
Source: arXiv
Published: 2026-11-17 05:00 UTC
URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18721
Source meta: preprint · primary · R4 · P5 · signal
Fetched: 2026-11-18 02:00 UTC

Attribution: arXiv [academic_research] https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18721

arXiv:2611.18721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid terahertz/infrared (THz/IR) links are usually modeled with Kolmogorov turbulence, but whether the turbulence spectral type matters equally for both bands has not been investigated. We transmit co-propagating 625 GHz and 1550 nm links through laboratory-controlled turbulence while a Mach-Zehnder interferometer and thermistors independently measure its spectral exponent and structure parameter on the shared path. Inlet-air temperature, not airflow speed, drives the exponent from Kolmogorov-like to non-Kolmogorov. At comparable structure parameters, this change reverses which model better reproduces the IR attenuation at the nominal inner scale, whereas the THz attenuation is insensitive to it. With type-matched models, predicted and measured bit-error-rate trends agree within 0.14 (IR) and 0.06 (THz) decades. IR predictions therefore require the spectral shape and inner scale, not turbulence strength alone.

### Some Considerations on Measuring and Comparing Things
Source: arXiv
Published: 2026-11-17 05:00 UTC
URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18724
Source meta: preprint · primary · R4 · P5 · signal
Fetched: 2026-11-18 02:00 UTC

Attribution: arXiv [academic_research] https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18724

arXiv:2611.18724v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Measurements and relationships between measurements are basic aspects underlying science and technology. In the present text, we present and discuss some of the approaches for measuring, normalizing, and comparing entities represented in terms of a set of measurements. Three main categories of measured values (constant, direct, or inverse) are proposed, underlaid by the relationship between data variation or intervals of interest and magnitude of the quantifications. For example, in certain cases the variation of measurements can be expected to be proportional to the relative magnitude (e.g.~when the magnitudes extend over long ranges). The considered approaches to comparing measurements include the Euclidean distance, three types of proximity based on the latter, as well as the Jaccard and coincidence indices. The presentation is complemented by graphical illustrations.

The world has never been wealthier. Yet in 2025, an estimated 831 million people lived on less than US$3 per day. This stark disparity exposes a systemic failure to translate global prosperity into basic security and opportunity for all. As slowing economic growth and multiple crises, such as conflict and climate change, undermine the momentum of global poverty reduction, governments now face a pressing test: whether they will still find, reach, and protect those already furthest behind, or allow them to fall deeper into poverty.

The Lancet Commission on the Health and Poverty Alleviation Initiative in China1 arrives at an important moment for global health. Progress towards universal health coverage (UHC) has slowed in many countries,2 with catastrophic health expenditure continuing to push households into poverty. Geopolitical conflict, faltering multilateralism, and economic factors such as inflation have made it more challenging to address global poverty eradication and health goals. The relationship between health and poverty has long been recognised, yet policy responses often remain fragmented.

A recent study finds the parasitoid wasp Tachinaephagus zealandicus to be a promising candidate for targeting the screwworm via biological control. AI agents can generate code at a scale that’s hard for humans to review line-by-line. PDD Kit helps ensure the code is doing what the developer intended by creating formal specifications and testing against them. It converts developer intent into a Verus specification, proves AI-generated code meets it for every input, and uses tests where proofs aren't practical. Developers review intent, not every line. The post Formally verifying agent-written full-stack web apps with PDD Kit appeared first on Microsoft Research.

Attribution: Simon Willison's Weblog [computing_cultures] https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/17/external-sandboxes-for-coding-agents/

External sandboxes for coding agents I've been exploring new ways to sandbox code that is executed by agents, with a focus on making it safer to try out local models without worrying that a mistake or prompt injection attack might cause them to take damaging actions on a machine. I worked on this project with Prime Radiant, the AI research lab behind Superpowers and other projects. My post on the Prime Radiant blog introduces the external sandbox pattern, where code executed by the agent runs inside a dedicated sandbox while the agent itself lives outside of that sandbox. To demonstrate this pattern we've released three sandbox server implementations: external-sandbox-v86 runs a Node.js server which then uses v86 to run Alpine Linux inside WebAssembly. external-sandbox-container is a Python web server which runs the sandbox in Alpine Linux inside an Apple Containers instance. external-sandbox-quicksand is another Python web server, this time using Microsoft's Quicksand sandboxing library, which bundles QEMU and Alpine Linux in a Python package!

hubie writes: Comets didn't seed life on Earth after all, a new study suggests, potentially overturning a century-old idea: The theory that comets delivered the molecular building blocks for life on Earth is a long-standing one, since comets are known to carry many of these molecules. However, a new study challenges this idea. The researchers, led by the University of Cambridge, found the cometary delivery of these building blocks would be – at best – a 'one-off fluke', and not the steady rain of prebiotic molecules that had been theorised. Using computer modelling, the researchers determined that comets travel too fast and at too sharp an angle to Earth's atmosphere for the fragile organic molecules to survive: they would almost certainly vaporise on impact with the surface. However, the researchers also found that another planet in our system – Mars – could be a slightly more promising candidate for cometary delivery of prebiotic molecules, although this is still highly unlikely. The results are published in the journal Scientific Reports.

Datasette Lite is my port of the Datasette Python application to run directly in the browser using WebAssembly and Pyodide. I've released a complete rewrite of Datasette Lite using service workers, and it's now almost indistinguishable from the real server-side application. You can now do all of the following, using a carefully crafted URL to lite.datasette.io: Load client-side Datasette to browse any SQLite database, JSON file, CSV file or SQL script Select a released version of Datasette to load from PyPI Load a specific commit, tag, or branch name from the Datasette GitHub repository Pick from over 100 versions of SQLite to use with Datasette Install additional Datasette plugins from PyPI or URLs to wheel files, including JavaScript visualization tools The ability to load specific Datasette references, plugins, and SQLite versions makes this a fantastic tool for linking to demos of work-in-progress features or bug reproductions, without needing to spin up a full web server to serve that demo. ### Redict deprecated in favor of Valkey
Source: LWN.net
Published: 2026-11-17 16:20 UTC
URL: https://lwn.net/Articles/1108155/
Source meta: specialist_media · specialist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-18 02:00 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: LWN.net [computing_cultures] https://lwn.net/Articles/1108155/

Drew DeVault has announced that Redict, a fork of Redis that was created in response to Redis's 2024 license change, has been deprecated. He recommends switching to Valkey, the permissively licensed Redis fork supported by the Linux Foundation. The two projects are mutually compatible, so switching should be as simple as changing which package is installed and renaming the configuration file. I had hoped to rally the Redis diaspora around a copyleft initiative, to protect ourselves from future rug-pulls, and made Redict to serve this purpose. However, with the valkey project's success, and Redis's return to a copyleft license, Redict was not able to build a sustainable community. We recommend that Redict users switch to valkey, which uses a permissive license but has better long-term prospects. We advise against switching back to Redis; though it is once again open source, and copyleft, it uses a contributor license agreement which will facilitate another rug-pull when Redis has a bad financial quarter.

Zellij is a relatively new entrant in the terminal-multiplexer category. Like GNU Screen and tmux it gives users the ability to manage a workspace inside a terminal with split panes, provides session management, and so forth; but Zellij also includes a web server for browser access to a terminal session, is extensible via a plugin API, and is likely more beginner-friendly than its predecessors. Its most recent release, version 0.46, adds a standalone terminal emulator, a built-in inbox for notifications, and a settings screen so users can configure the application without fussing with configuration files. While the low version number might suggest that it is not yet ready for serious use, it seems stable and full-featured enough to meet the needs of many users.

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Martin Fowler [computing_cultures] https://martinfowler.com/articles/deterministic-simulation-testing.html

Distributed systems are hard to test because partial failures overlap with live traffic and the same fault can produce different execution traces on different runs. Unmesh Joshi describes how deterministic simulation testing addresses this by replacing real clocks, networks, and storage with simulated components driven by a single-threaded execution loop. This allows simulating both hard failures and routine slowdowns—such as network and disk latency spikes—and more importantly makes every execution reproducible. This article explains the technique using a quorum key-value store as a running example, with code from Tickloom, a Java implementation of the approach. more…

For example, consumers perceive a $100 check for overtime work differently than a $100 tax refund. One is seen as earned, and the other as a discretionary bonus. A new study of 5,589 participants across 21 countries finds evidence that this concept still holds true. [...] The researchers say they were uncertain whether the mental accounting concept would hold up in the current environment, in which technology has completely changed our relationship with money and how we spend it. For example, the norm now is to receive both overtime pay and tax rebates via direct deposit. "Considering major changes in how we receive and spend money, especially with the proliferation of automated digital payments, a large, robust study of the concept of mental accounting was not only appropriate, it was necessary," says Ruggeri. "Fnord666" writes: ULA suffers first outright failure with loss of Vulcan rocket carrying 40 Amazon Leo satellites: In a major setback for United Launch Alliance, the company's new heavy-lift Vulcan rocket carrying a batch of Amazon Leo internet satellites, malfunctioned during the climb to space Sunday, dooming the payload and throwing a costly wrench into the launch schedule of both companies. "Based on data received by our Launch Director, we confirm that the Vulcan vehicle launched from Space Launch Complex 41 (at the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station) suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit," ULA said in a statement some 50 minutes after liftoff. "We will work closely with our customer and other appropriate organizations to find the cause, determine the appropriate corrective action and return to flight as quickly as possible." It was the first outright failure of a United Launch Alliance rocket since the company, a partnership between Boeing and Lockheed Martin, was formed in 2006.

Release: llm 0.37.3 A bug fix release for LLM, mainly to cover a problem with the most recent Homebrew package of the software. Homebrew now ships the latest SQLite, 3.54.1, which includes a fix that broke LLM's logging code. Short version: in SQLite 3.54.0 the following SQL: select json_object('a', (select json_array(1))) Returns this: {"a":[1]} But in 3.54.1 the same query returns this: {"a":"[1]"} According to D. Richard Hipp: That was a bug fix. Per the documentation, (SELECT json_array(...)) returns SQL text, not JSON. Hence the 3.54.1 behavior is correct and 3.54.0 was a bug. The workaround looks like this: select json_object('a', json((select json_array(1)))) Tags: llm, webassembly, sqlite, generative-ai, ai, llms, d-richard-hipp

Futexes are a kernel subsystem that provides support for fast mutexes in user space. While futexes can indeed be fast, they are not fast enough for a number of users. Partly as a result of that, the implementation of futexes has grown in complexity over the years, with two basic variants on offer. The desire for faster futexes remains, though, and that inspires new patches, including this series from Suleiman Souhlal adding a third futex class called "futex PING" for "priority inheritance next generation".

Frank Vandermeiren has announced the creation of the Manjaro Project e.V., a nonprofit organization in Germany that is independent of the Manjaro GmbH & Co KG company. This is following a governance struggle that took place earlier this year between a number of Manjaro Linux contributors and Philip Müller, project lead and CEO of the Manjaro company. At the moment, we are still working on optimizing the new development infrastructure, which was partly necessitated by the ongoing (A.I.) bot attacks against our old infrastructure. However, as you may have noticed, the last Testing Updates and Stable Updates were initiated by the Manjaro Team without supervision from Philip Müller — with special thanks to @Yochanan for his hard work! Dennis ten Hoove has indicated that "a transfer of company assets to the e.V. has not yet taken place", and the group's next step is to ready the nonprofit for the transition and "reach out and engage in dialogue with the company".

### Bliki: Generated Glossary
Source: Martin Fowler
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://martinfowler.com/bliki/GeneratedGlossary.html
Source meta: specialist_media · specialist · R5 · P5 · baseline
Updated: 2026-11-12 14:15 UTC
Fetched: 2026-11-18 02:00 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Martin Fowler [computing_cultures] https://martinfowler.com/bliki/GeneratedGlossary.html

When we use LLMs in a specialized domain, such as the operations of any reasonably-large organization, there is a lot of specialized vocabulary. Such words and specialized meanings will be foreign to an LLM because they aren't in its training set, making it harder for the LLM to be effective when doing tasks in that domain. One technique to aid this is to use an LLM to generate a glossary of the terminology in that domain, and make this glossary available for any LLMs doing work in those circumstances. The sources for the LLM can be any material within the organization concerned such as documents, emails, and chat logs. In some cases getting transcripts of audio or video may be helpful, although most organizations generate enough text to do the job. The glossary-generating LLM should look for single words, and phrases of several words that regularly hang out together to form a meaningful term. The generator should be asked to identify terms that are new to it, but also known terms that are being used in unfamiliar ways. The latter can often cause the most confusion.

Automated testing in the age of AI coding assistants is problematic: when AI agents write both production and test code, developers risk losing the assurance that automated tests protect against functional errors. Matteo Vaccari makes three claims: (1) when AI writes the code, developers become its customers; (2) therefore customer tests, not developer tests, become the primary contract between humans and AI; (3) moving that contract into test data rather than test code makes it easier to protect it from unexpected modifications by coding agents. All of this optimizes for human-readable tests that establish a contract between humans and AI. While in the past DSL parsers and custom test runners were expensive to write and maintain, now AI makes them cheap. more…

It’s that time of the year when the November Thoughtworks Technology Radar appears. Again my colleagues have taken a sweep of the technologies that our teams have used in the field, and pulled together a summary of what’s popped up in the last six months. It’s been a busy half-year, one that again has been dominated by AI, and that’s reflected in the many AI blips on the radar. The mass of blips makes it hard to develop a coherent story around trends, but Chris Ford has done a fine job of the writing the accompanying article on macro trends. One team of passionate people experimenting with agents can make almost anything work. They share a context, a credit card and a mental model. They review each other’s work because they sit together, and they know what to check and how much latitude to give the coding agent. Two hundred people, though, cannot work that way. The moment agentic AI becomes an operating model rather than a pilot, a second layer of problems appears: How is context shared between teams? What’s the token bill? How do we deal with increased review demands?

Long-horizon agents can automate complex tasks that take days or weeks to complete and involve multiple exchanges with people and external systems. Many things can go wrong during this time, including process crashes, network failures, and unanticipated real-world behavior. Kiran Prakash explains durable execution: an emerging pattern that helps agents recover from these failures and move towards their goal. In this programming model, the runtime keeps a record of the result of each step that interacts with the outside world so that, when a failure occurs, the program runs again, completed steps are skipped, and the program's state is rebuilt from the record. more…

Hello! I’ve been working on a Django site recently, and I decided to use SQLite as the database. When I was getting started with using SQLite as database for a website I read a bunch of blog posts about how it is totally fine to use SQLite in production for a small site and I think it is totally fine, but what I did not fully appreciate is that SQLite is still a database, databases are complicated, and I do not know a lot about operating databases. So here are a couple of small things I’ve been learning about running SQLite. This is the 4th website I’ve used SQLite for, and I think this one is harder because with the power of the Django ORM I’ve been making the database do more work than I was previously without Django. I started by turning on WAL mode like all the blog posts said to do and hoping for the best. ANALYZE is apparently important Today I was running a query (using SQLite’s FTS5 for full-text search) on a table with 4000 rows and it took 5 seconds. That seemed wrong to me: computers are fast! It turned out that what I needed to do was to run ANALYZE!

Hello! One of my long term projects on here is figuring out how to write frontend Javascript without using Node or any other server JS runtime. One issue I run into a lot in my frontend JS projects is that I don’t know how to write tests for them. I’ve tried to use Playwright in the past, but it felt slow and unwieldy to be starting these new browser processes all the time, and it involved some Node code to orchestrate the tests. The result is that I just don’t test my frontend code which doesn’t feel great. Usually I don’t update my projects much either so it doesn’t come up that much, but it would be nice to be able to make changes with more confidence! So a way to do frontend testing that I like has been on my wishlist for a long time. idea: just run the tests in the browser tab Alex Chan wrote a great post a while back called Testing JavaScript without a (third-party) framework in response to one of my previous posts in this series that explained how to write a tiny unit-testing framework that runs in a page in browser.

I watched the discussion on agentic loops grow louder over the past few months. But for me, the reality is simpler: prompt engineering has shifted from individual tasks to systems design, and the harness around the model (not the model itself) is now my primary constraint in software engineering. Not all tasks are equal You can categorize the work that we give to our agents into five distinct tiers, scaling from a quick question up through Agile tasks, stories, and epics to a continuous system: A simple question: This does not require an agent; an assistant can answer it. Attribution: Vercel Blog [platforms_infrastructure] https://vercel.com/changelog/vercel-blob-now-supports-ttls-for-automatic-deletion

Vercel Blob can now delete blobs automatically. Pass ttlDays when you write a blob and it is deleted that many days after upload, from 1 to 730 days. The TTL counts from the blob's upload date. Use TTLs for blobs you would otherwise delete yourself, such as session transcripts, exports, and temporary uploads. ttlDays works on put(), copy(), putImage(), multipart uploads, and presigned upload URLs. Every write result and head() response now includes expiresAt, so you know when a blob is due for deletion. setTtl() changes or removes the TTL of blobs you already have, one URL or up to 1,000 at a time, without re-uploading them. In Vercel CLI 65.16.0 and later, pass --ttl-days to vercel blob put, put-image, copy or presign, and use vercel blob set-ttl on existing blobs. Setting a TTL costs one Advanced Operation per started 60 days, on top of the write. A 7-day TTL costs one, and the 730-day maximum costs 13. Clearing a TTL and the deletions themselves are free. You can track TTL operations in the Blob section of the Observability tab. npm install @vercel/blob@2.9.
